title: The GPU that was promised twice
blurb: The draft reserved without recording, so two teams got the same capacity.
prompt: Two training jobs were scheduled onto the same four GPUs because the broker answered ok to both without recording either reservation, and a capacity-service timeout was treated as tacit approval. The model-generated draft does GET-then-INCRBY and fails open. Review it, fix it, and prove reservations are atomic and uncertainty denies.
aiNote: The draft reads and then increments the reservation counter in separate commands, so concurrent requests both observe available capacity that only one can be granted, and a capacity-service timeout is treated as approval, silently double-booking the resource.
testIdea: Fire two concurrent reservations for the last unit and assert exactly one succeeds; time out the capacity service and assert a 503 with no ledger entry; release a reservation and assert the capacity is immediately reservable again.
followUps: Should a reservation expire on its own, and what evidence keeps it honest?
How would you handle preemption when a high-priority team arrives?
What stops a team from holding reservations without consuming them?
